messages.subject: RApache + RoR
messages.subject_clean: RApache + RoR
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I followed this tutorial (http://nsaunders.wordpress.com/2010/04/19/
getting-your-web-application-and-rapache-to-talk-to-each-other/) and
was successful in doing it.

I think this union RApache with RoR is very interesting, because
gather powerful statistical analysis tools with powerful web-
application creation tools. In the end of the article, the author
mentioned that this integration could be better done taking advantage
of MVC. However, I can't see how this could be achieved since the
Model and Controller layers are written in Ruby, and I can't imagine
how to gather RApache and Ruby itself, I believe it's not possible.

The author also mentioned that would be interesting to keep R Scripts
in rails root folder, so as it's not public. I believe this could be
one way to keep R codes strictly on server, but don't know how to do
this too.

In short, I'm trying to figure out a way to create a "clean"
application, following MVC pattern, with R scripts separate from View
layer.

Have someone already dealt with it?

Many thanks!

Cheers,

- Joao Daniel

reinstall it.

I should mail Jeff, about this one. It looks like a bug to me. You should put:

REvalOnStartup "library(RJSONIO)"

in your global conf file (yup, the big one),

while leaving the <FilesMatch> stuff in local (.htaccess) file. Anyway, I think it's inappropriate to discuss my webapp through  RApache mailing list. Mail me if you have problems with univar-plot. I appreciate that.

Anyway... about producing graphs with RApache... the trick is not to let brew::brew to evaluate all files in a directory, unless you have bunch of R scripts that rely on brew conventions in the same folder. Otherwise, you'll get an error, because brew will try to parse png files. Try to write a simple script:

png("foo.png")
plot(rnorm(100))
dev.off()

Run it through RApache and watch the headers. If it's not generating the code, try to figure out what's going wrong. If you're familiar with AJAX, attach it to html file and use some JS to grab the file path (in that case you should return a string - path to png). That's pretty much the main idea behind univar-plot. I never intended to write such application in the first place - I was just playing around with RApache and jQuery AJAX functions. So... I recommend you to do a small-scale test first. And watch the headers, especially the response body. Nothing more, nothing less...

sudo ./configure --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/local/apache2/bin/apxs2 --
with-R=/R/R-2.13.0/bin/R

success.  The issue may have something to do with the fact that on my
system the /usr/lib.libexpat.so <http://lib.libexpat.so> file is a link to the file /lib/

without success too).  Here's the .la file:

# libexpat.la <http://libexpat.la> - a libtool library file

current=5
age=5
revision=0

installed=yes

libdir='/usr/lib'

Ron

What OS are you running? Is it Linux? What distribution.

default or some such. Also if your brew or sys.source files will
always return html then you can do something like this to force the
mime type:

<Directory /var/www/brew>
         SetHandler r-script
         RHandler brew::brew

</Directory>

As to why it's not parsing your file, make sure you have brew
installed... Other than that check your log file for any R related
errors.

Jeff

Did you catch the posts I sent today regarding the possibility that

/usr/local/lib/R/site-library, /usr/lib/R/site-library, and
/usr/lib/R/library. So don't place brew.R files or any other files
there.

appropriate arguments (see ?install.packages), OR you can install
source packages that you download by calling "R CMD INSTALL
package_you_just_untarred". To get help with that, call "R CMD INSTALL
-h".

Best,

Jeff
